import pandas as pd

# Read source tables with index_col=0 to ignore the numerical index column
source0 = pd.read_csv("autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/intermediate_space/length2_72/training_0.csv", index_col=0)
source1 = pd.read_csv("autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/intermediate_space/length2_72/training_1.csv", index_col=0)

# Join on 'city'
joined = pd.merge(source0, source1, on="city", how="inner")

# Select and reorder columns to match target schema: ['type', 'fare', 'ride_id', 'driver_count']
# Convert types to match target schema
result = joined[['type', 'fare', 'ride_id', 'driver_count']].copy()

# Ensure correct dtypes
result['type'] = result['type'].astype(str)
result['fare'] = result['fare'].astype(float)
result['ride_id'] = result['ride_id'].astype(int)
result['driver_count'] = result['driver_count'].astype(int)

# Write to target path
result.to_csv("autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length2_72/target_multisource.csv", index=False)

import pandas as pd

# Read source tables
source0 = pd.read_csv("autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length2_72/training_0.csv", index_col=0)
source1 = pd.read_csv("autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length2_72/training_1.csv", index_col=0)

# Join on city
joined = pd.merge(source0, source1, on="city", how="inner")

# Rename columns to match target schema
# source1.type -> type (already named)
# source0.fare -> fare
# source0.ride_id -> ride_id
# source1.driver_count -> driver_count

# Group by 'type' (primary key), aggregate sums of fare, ride_id, driver_count
result = joined.groupby("type", as_index=False).agg({
    "fare": "sum",
    "ride_id": "sum",
    "driver_count": "sum"
})

# Write output
result.to_csv("autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length2_72/target_multisource_critique_history.csv", index=False)
